items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I gave him the Duke Ellington things... Al Cohn, I gave him the Duke Ellington things

ctx.x: Did some of the fellas that were into that suffer later on? Even if they got over it?

They — Stan Getz, Zoot Sims, Al Cohn and Serge Chaloff all died I think from cirrhosis of the liver. Even though they quit. Even when they quit though, they were all drinking. Stan Getz would drink a fifth of liquor and it wouldn’t bother him like it would the guy who never made that. But they were all straight later on. But I think what happened is it affected them. It stays in your system I suppose. Thank God I never did that, and let me tell you one of the reasons. Two things. I like to laugh. And all the…
It must have been hard for Woody to deal with that.

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: But if Johnny Mandel was alive or Al Cohn or Manny Albam, these great arrangers, they would tell you they learned arranging from what Tiny was doing.

ctx.x: Everybody in the world has one. So, and you could relate to all, and all kids who play in the streets could relate to my stories, you know. So and I was lucky to have a great childhood. I grew up with Tiny Kahn, see Tiny Kahn is when I was from 6 years old until I went in the Army at 19 or 18, until I got with Woody Herman’s band really. We were together day and night. And if you can, people who know these names can imagine what we looked like at 15 years old, we looked like Peter Lorre and Sydney Greenstreet…
